Dollar values ride the annual FFY dollar-table cycle in ODJFS's Food Assistance Change Transmittal series (currently Transmittal No. 105, effective 10/1/2025), which this pass confirmed matches the SUA figures already independently verified in packages/snap-rules' states.ts. Two entries below record genuine, primary-source-confirmed DISCREPANCIES against that already-verified engine entry — not routine COLA-cycle warnings — and are the load-bearing content of this pack.

entries.warning: Ohio's FFY26 dollar figures (Standard Utility Allowance $766, Limited Utility Allowance $479, Single Standard Utility Allowance $108, Single Telephone Allowance $46, Standard Deduction $209/$223/$261/$299, Excess Shelter cap $744, Homeless Shelter Deduction $198, resource limits $3,000/$4,500) are all sourced from Food Assistance Change Transmittal No. 105, effective 10/1/2025 — due for the October 2026 COLA update. Find the successor transmittal (the next dated Food Assistance Change Transmittal at emanuals.jfs.ohio.gov) before quoting any Ohio dollar amount after this date.

DISCREPANCY vs the already-verified snap-rules engine constant: states.ts records OH bbce_threshold_pct=130 ("BBCE at the FEDERAL 130% ... the same archetype as Georgia ... waives the asset test without raising the income screen"). This pack's direct read of OAC 5101:4-2-02 (effective 10/1/2024, confirmed via a raw authenticated-PDF fetch after a summarizing tool gave contradictory paraphrases) found a genuine 200% FPL broad-based categorical-eligibility pathway — "Ohio careline" — that waives the 130% gross test, the net income test, AND the resource limit for any household at or below 200% FPL that receives the (routine, notice-plus-text-message) Careline notification at application or recertification. This is NOT reflected in the 130% engine constant. Re-verify OAC 5101:4-2-02 directly and resolve which figure the engine should carry before this date; this pack does not touch packages/snap-rules and does not resolve the discrepancy itself.

DISCREPANCY vs the already-verified snap-rules engine constant: states.ts records OH abawd_waiver_avail=true. This pack found Ohio Revised Code § 5101.548(B), effective September 30, 2025 (enacted via HB 96), STATUTORILY PROHIBITS ODJFS from requesting, applying for, or renewing any ABAWD geographic waiver going forward. Independently corroborated: as of this pack's build date, USDA's current ABAWD waiver tracking and the independent abawdmap.us tracker both show Ohio with NO active waiver anywhere in the state. Re-verify ORC § 5101.548 and the current FNS ABAWD waiver list directly before this date and resolve which value the engine should carry; this pack does not touch packages/snap-rules and does not resolve the discrepancy itself.

OAC 5101:4-4-03(A)(6) excludes vehicles "in accordance with Ohio's temporary assistance for needy families (TANF) plan" under Pub. L. 106-387 § 847, but does not itself state how many vehicles are excluded or any per-vehicle equity-value exclusion dollar figure — those mechanics live in Ohio's TANF state plan, which this pack did not fetch directly. Pull Ohio's current TANF state plan (jfs.ohio.gov) before building calculator logic on a specific vehicle-exclusion count or dollar figure.

This pack's fetch of OAC 5101:4-5-03 (certification periods) did not itself define the "Annual Reporter" simplified-reporting status or spell out its exact mid-certification renewal interaction with the 36-month zero-earned-income elderly/disabled certification tier. Confirm the interaction directly against OAC 5101:4-5-03 and 5101:4-6-29 before relying on a specific renewal-timing claim for that household type.
